method: Feedforward, recurrent, seq2seq and TCN comparison
result: Gated RNNs handle irregular household load better than simple RNNs; rankings depend on aggregation.
relevance: Closest task match; motivates identical splits and architecture comparison. Their sampling differs from ours.
reference: A. Gasparin, S. Lukovic, and C. Alippi, "Deep Learning for Time Series Forecasting: The Electric Load Case," arXiv:1907.09207, 2019.

result: TCNs generally achieve better forecasting accuracy and less hyperparameter sensitivity in the reported experiments.
relevance: Motivates the convolutional family. Our pooled CNN is simpler than their dilated TCN.
reference: P. Lara-Benitez, M. Carranza-Garcia, J. M. Luna-Romera, and J. C. Riquelme, "Temporal Convolutional Networks Applied to Energy-Related Time Series Forecasting," Applied Sciences, vol. 10, no. 7, art. 2322, 2020.

result: Identifies uncertainty, overfitting, data requirements and distribution changes as open problems.
relevance: Frames limitations of a single-house, single-seed comparison; no directly comparable experiment.
reference: A. Casolaro, V. Capone, G. Iannuzzo, and F. Camastra, "Deep Learning for Time Series Forecasting: Advances and Open Problems," Information, vol. 14, no. 11, art. 598, 2023.

result: Reports improved forecasting versus tested alternatives, with a complex training procedure.
relevance: Possible hybrid extension; solar generation differs from household consumption and results cannot be transferred.
reference: E. M. Al-Ali et al., "Solar Energy Production Forecasting Based on a Hybrid CNN-LSTM-Transformer Model," Mathematics, vol. 11, no. 3, art. 676, 2023.

result: Convolutional networks outperform canonical recurrent networks on diverse tasks and show longer effective memory.
relevance: Supports testing CNNs without assuming LSTM superiority; benchmark tasks differ from our load task.
reference: S. Bai, J. Z. Kolter, and V. Koltun, "An Empirical Evaluation of Generic Convolutional and Recurrent Networks for Sequence Modeling," arXiv:1803.01271, 2018.

result: Strong forecasting with fully connected layers; interpretable and generic variants outperform evaluated benchmarks.
relevance: Justifies retaining an MLP baseline. Our plain MLP does not implement N-BEATS residual decomposition.
reference: B. N. Oreshkin, D. Carpov, N. Chapados, and Y. Bengio, "N-BEATS: Neural basis expansion analysis for interpretable time series forecasting," ICLR, 2020.

result: Reduces attention cost to O(L log L) and reports improved long-sequence forecasting.
relevance: Attention extension for longer contexts; its long-horizon benchmarks differ from this 24-hour setting.
reference: H. Zhou et al., "Informer: Beyond Efficient Transformer for Long Sequence Time-Series Forecasting," AAAI, 2021.

dataset: Six benchmarks spanning energy, traffic, weather and other domains
result: Reports improved long-term forecasting by learning periodic subseries dependencies.
relevance: Motivates explicit seasonal baselines and future decomposition experiments; no direct household score comparison.
reference: H. Wu, J. Xu, J. Wang, and M. Long, "Autoformer: Decomposition Transformers with Auto-Correlation for Long-Term Series Forecasting," NeurIPS, 2021.

result: Simple linear models outperform the tested Transformer alternatives under the paper's protocol.
relevance: Counters complexity-only model choice; supports persistence controls and cautious performance claims.
reference: A. Zeng, M. Chen, L. Zhang, and Q. Xu, "Are Transformers Effective for Time Series Forecasting?" arXiv:2205.13504, 2022.

dataset: Multivariate long-term benchmarks, including electricity and weather
result: Patching reduces attention memory and improves forecasting versus evaluated Transformer models.
relevance: A possible fourth family for later work, requiring separate tuning; not implemented or claimed in this study.
reference: Y. Nie, N. H. Nguyen, P. Sinthong, and J. Kalagnanam, "A Time Series is Worth 64 Words: Long-term Forecasting with Transformers," ICLR, 2023.
G. Hebrail and A. Berard, Individual Household Electric Power Consumption, UCI Machine Learning Repository, 2012, doi: 10.24432/C58K54.
